target.title: feat: expose provider-scoped model usage independently of diagnostics
target.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97149

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw computes trusted model usage token counts and estimated cost, but provider plugins do not have a narrow supported contract for consuming usage from the providers they own. Using the diagnostics stream would expose a broader internal surface and would incorrectly require operators to enable diagnostics just to support provider-owned usage accounting.

This change is intentionally constrained to two purposes:

1. A plugin service can receive model usage only for an exact normalized provider ID uniquely registered by that same plugin. Events for other providers, missing providers, or provider IDs with ambiguous ownership are not delivered.
2. Plugin model usage is separately and explicitly enabled with `plugins.modelUsage.enabled: true`. It works when `diagnostics.enabled` is `false`; diagnostics remains independently controlled even though both paths share core model usage instrumentation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway-started plugin services receive `ctx.modelUsage?.onEvent(...)` only when the model usage plugin feed is enabled. Core model usage emitters can fan the same accounting facts to diagnostics when diagnostics is enabled and to provider plugins when model usage delivery is enabled, without making either setting depend on the other.

The service context derives uniquely owned provider IDs from the loaded plugin registry and filters every event before delivery. This is not a cross-provider analytics feed: registering a service alone does not grant model usage access, and normalized provider-ID collisions fail closed.

The public event contains provider/model/session attribution, token buckets, context facts, duration, and `costUsd` when available. It does not expose raw prompts, responses, tool payloads, or the broader internal diagnostics stream.

## User Impact

Provider plugin authors can build provider-specific token accounting, quota, or cost integrations without enabling diagnostics or receiving data belonging to other providers. Operators retain separate explicit control over diagnostics and plugin model usage delivery.

AI-assisted: yes, Codex.
